title.zh: India starts tokenizing $620 billion corporate bond market with digital rupee settlement
title.en: India starts tokenizing $620 billion corporate bond market with digital rupee settlement

current_state.zh: 印度已启动 Demat 2.0 代币化公司债试点，首批三家发行人合计发行约1.07亿美元，第一阶段发行仍在进行，后续阶段将引入二级交易和零售投资者。
current_state.en: India has launched the Demat 2.0 tokenized corporate bond pilot, with three issuers raising about $107 million; first-phase issuances remain ongoing, and later phases are planned to add secondary trading and retail access.

updates.what_changed_zh: India has begun tokenizing its $620 billion corporate bond market using digital rupee settlement, marking a major state-backed step toward blockchain-based financial market infrastructure.

updates.title_zh: India launches tokenized bond pilot with $107M issued
updates.title_en: India launches tokenized bond pilot with $107M issued
updates.what_changed_zh: 印度证券交易委员会（SEBI）与印度储备银行正式启动 Demat 2.0 代币化公司债试点；REC、Larsen & Toubro 和 IIFL 合计发行 102.5 亿卢比（约1.07亿美元），通过分布式账本与批发型 CBDC 结算。
updates.what_changed_en: SEBI and RBI formally launched the Demat 2.0 tokenized corporate bond pilot; REC, Larsen & Toubro and IIFL issued a combined 10.25 billion rupees (~$107 million) on distributed ledger infrastructure linked to wholesale CBDC settlement.
updates.current_state_zh: 印度已启动 Demat 2.0 代币化公司债试点，首批三家发行人合计发行约1.07亿美元，第一阶段发行仍在进行，后续阶段将引入二级交易和零售投资者。
updates.current_state_en: India has launched the Demat 2.0 tokenized corporate bond pilot, with three issuers raising about $107 million; first-phase issuances remain ongoing, and later phases are planned to add secondary trading and retail access.
updates.detailed_summary_zh: India's SEBI and RBI launched the Demat 2.0 tokenized corporate bond pilot, with REC, Larsen & Toubro, and IIFL issuing a combined 10.25 billion rupees (~$107 million) on distributed ledger infrastructure linked to the RBI's wholesale CBDC.
updates.detailed_summary_en: India's SEBI and RBI launched the Demat 2.0 tokenized corporate bond pilot, with REC, Larsen & Toubro, and IIFL issuing a combined 10.25 billion rupees (~$107 million) on distributed ledger infrastructure linked to the RBI's wholesale CBDC.
